subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should timed-out deferred maintenance preserve the existing single-flight same-session plugin lifecycle, or should OpenClaw deliberately require all existing context engines to support overlapping `maintain()` calls?
rationale: The patch’s host-side fence cannot serialize plugin-owned work, so choosing to permit overlap changes the effective contract of an existing extensibility seam rather than being only an internal timeout implementation detail.

options.title: Preserve serial plugin invocation
options.body: Keep the timeout’s lane release and host-write fence, but defer or coalesce later maintenance until the earlier same-session `maintain()` call settles.

options.title: Adopt concurrent maintenance
options.body: Accept re-entrant same-session `maintain()` as the permanent plugin contract and provide an explicit compatibility/versioning path for existing engines.

options.title: Pause the timeout change
options.body: Leave the existing lifecycle unchanged until the plugin contract and cancellation strategy are designed together.

recommendation.title: Preserve serial plugin invocation
recommendation.body: Keep the timeout’s lane release and host-write fence, but defer or coalesce later maintenance until the earlier same-session `maintain()` call settles.
